messages:
alice.wu: Quick follow-up from the office hours — we need a small design doc for the eviction-handshake + stable-burst lane idea. TL;DR: allow short-lived prewarm capacity that doesn't force global rebalances but still lets an operator safely evict when needed.

mateo.g: curious how this differs from the existing burst-credit approach?

priya.k: +1 on documenting. My take: burst credits are accounting-focused (who pays). Stable-burst is about a dedicated admission lane that can be torn down without moving tenant state (no KV-cache migrations). Basically ephemeral pools that keep warm KV caches per-tenant.

benjamin: right — the problem today is when we prewarm nodes we end up with stuck leases and big global rebalances if we evict. Need a handshake so runtimes can gracefully drop cached state.

alice.wu: proposal sketch: admission service returns a lease with (lease_id, lane_type, ttl, graceful_drain_window). Operator can request a graceful_drain(lease_id) which signals the runtime to finish inflight requests, flush or checkpoint KV-cache, and then acknowledge. If no ack within graceful_drain_window, operator forcibly reclaims.

mateo.g: handshake API sounds good. Small nit: we should make lane_type enum include {stable, burst_ephemeral, reserved}. "stable" means long-lived and holds state we must migrate; "burst_ephemeral" means we can drop without heavy migration.

priya.k: agree. Also: make graceful_drain_window configurable per-tenant and per-lane. Some customers have huge KV-caches and need extra time, others want fast reclaim. Default 30s, max 10m.

benjamin: operationally we need metrics: lease_state, drain_requested_ts, ack_ts, forced_reclaim_count, avg_drain_time. Add alerts for ack latency > 2x SLO.

alice.wu: admission + operator boundary: admission API stays central to scheduling decisions. Autoscaler/operator decides to scale down nodes and issues graceful_drain(lease_id)s in parallel. Avoid operator owning per-request routing. Operator should not decide per-request admission.

mateo.g: +1. Keep operator responsibilities: capacity provisioning, node lifecycle, drain orchestration. Keep admission service responsible for fairness, tenant quotas, borrowing tokens.

priya.k: corner case: what if runtime acknowledges drain but then is slow to actually free GPU memory due to pinned CUDA contexts? We should define two-phase reclaim: ACK -> start background eviction -> when GPU memory released, send RECLAIM_COMPLETE. Operator can wait for RECLAIM_COMPLETE or force-kill after deadline.

alice.wu: agreed. Documenting handshake sequence:
```
1) OP: drain_request(lease_id)
2) RT: ack_drain(lease_id)
3) RT: stop_accepting_new_burst_requests(lane)
4) RT: finish_inflight_requests(timeout)
5) RT: checkpoint_or_drop_kvcache(if lane==stable)
6) RT: release_gpu_memory -> reclaim_complete(lease_id)
```

benjamin: for burst_ephemeral lanes step 5 is a no-op (drop cache) which makes reclaim faster. Nice.

mateo.g: admission semantics: reserve returns a soft_capacity and a hard_capacity. Soft is guaranteed but can be preempted with graceful drain. Hard is best-effort. That helps tenants plan fallback to cheaper models.

priya.k: we should also add a small token for prewarm-count and a boolean hot_path. Admission response: {lease_id, lane, ttl, soft_capacity, hard_capacity, hot_path:true/false}. Keep field names snake_case in proto.

alice.wu: implementation notes: operator needs a drain coordinator that batches drain_requests to avoid thundering herd on reclaim. E.g., prefer draining 10% of burst nodes per minute, pick nodes with lowest active soft_capacity.

benjamin: batching + backoff is important. Also consider a backpressure signal from the admission service: if admission RT cannot allocate new leases because headroom low, it should expose headroom_pct metric; operator uses that to decide whether to allocate more GPUs or trigger canary bursts.

mateo.g: decision point: should autoscaler be allowed to call admission.reserve when provisioning new nodes to warm them up? That couples autoscaler to admission internals. I prefer an explicit prewarm API on operator that requests 'prewarm intent' and the admission service marks capacity as prewarming for accounting.

priya.k: agreed — explicit prewarm intent keeps boundaries clearer. API: prewarm_intent(tenant_id, model_hint, desired_gpus) -> intent_id, expected_ready_ts. Operator polls intent status.

alice.wu: fallback policies: if reclaim stalls past max_grace, route long-running requests to fallback model or cheaper lane. Add routing rules in the console to set per-tenant fallback.

benjamin: can we add a small config DSL for lane policies? E.g.
```
lane_policy: {
  name: "burst_ephemeral",
  max_ttl: 600,
  max_concurrent_leases: 50,
  drain_window: 30
}
```
This can live in tenant config.

mateo.g: one more edge: cross-region tenant workloads. If prewarm is region-specific, admission must tag leases with region and operator must avoid cross-region reclaims that break affinity. Document that region-affinity is immutable for a lease's lifespan.

priya.k: +1. Also add a metric for cross_region_rejects so we can measure inefficiencies.

alice.wu: next steps: I'll draft a short RFC with sequence diagrams and the proto sketches (ReserveLease, PrewarmIntent, DrainRequest, ReclaimComplete). @mateo.g please capture the operator batching algorithm, @priya.k please list metrics/alert thresholds, @benjamin please prototype a minimal ack flow in the runtime shim.

orch-bot: deploy:starting - rolling out admission-service/eviction-handshake:v0.1 -> canary 3 nodes

benjamin: noted, I'll try the shim on the canary nodes and report latency on reclaim. If we see > 5s median for ephemeral lanes that's a problem.

mateo.g: sgtm. Also we should add e2e test that simulates heavy prewarm + mass reclaim to catch thundering herd.

alice.wu: thanks all — I'll post the RFC draft in #eng-runtime by EOD and tag reviewers."
